mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following two consecutive quarters of GDP decline, or if the correlation between GDP declines and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity boosts economic growth and related sectors.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the periods following sustained HOUST increases, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL on negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is a major driver of economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
